correctness.rationale: Tikhomirov's actual Theorem 2.3 supplies bounded continuous fields h,k with the two claimed semiconjugacy equations and uniform sup bounds. For H=Id+h on R^n, H^-1(C) closed and bounded for every compact C, hence compact; H is proper. For arbitrary y choose R>||y||+||h||∞, and homotope x-y to x+h(x)-y on B_R; nonzero boundary gives Brouwer degree 1, implying H(x)=y. Ditto K=Id+k. Pullback H^-1(C) of any nonempty compact forward g-invariant subsystem C is compact, nonempty and forward f-invariant; restriction H is an onto compact factor map, so htop(g|C)≤htop(f|H^-1(C)). Taking suprema yields h_cpt(g)≤h_cpt(f), and K gives the reverse. Empty family convention in [0,∞] is 0 on both sides since factors transfer compact subsystems. No injectivity, inverse identity, Bowen entropy or whole-noncompact entropy is claimed. This is a complete finite-dimensional degree and factor proof, not a numerical certificate.
risks: Only finite n and compact-subsystem topological entropy, no injectivity or structural stability.
